qa.answer: Four options. Reallocate 400 released seals from WO-2615 and return the rejected batch (no incremental cost, no slip, recommended), accept the rejected batch under concession (no cost but high airworthiness risk after a durometer failure), air freight from Ohio Valley Seal (USD 109.8K including LDs, lands 25 Oct, still 11 days beyond float), or wait for the Daejeon replacement (USD 54K of LDs, Halcyra moves 6 days).

The reallocation is the cheapest at no incremental cost: the seals are already released stock, Daejeon credits the USD 34K rejected batch, and the replacement backfills WO-2615 at the original USD 85 price. Only if the replacement also fails do we release the Ohio Valley backstop, which adds USD 10.8K of price premium at USD 112 a seal.

In 2024 a batch of O-ring seals failed durometer checks at receiving and short-shipped an engine kit (PRE-09). We reallocated released stock from a later work order and backfilled it from the US source for USD 9.8K; the induction held and the later work order was backfilled two weeks before need. The lesson was that reallocation is the fastest lever when a later work order holds released stock of the same batch family.

WO-2608 inducts on Engine shop line E-17 on 10 Oct and needs 400 SEA-3100-510 seals, but all 400 in batch DSL-26-0918 failed receiving inspection. Without the reallocation the next good seals are Daejeon's replacement on 20 Oct, a 10 day slip against 4 days of float, so the Halcyra Airways redelivery moves 6 days from 11 Dec to 17 Dec.
